title: Construction and uniqueness of the coordinate Euler polynomial over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq0$, and $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_0,\ldots,z_n])$ a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-proj]. Put $\mathcal O_X(d)=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_k}(d)$ for $d\in\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $X$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and Noetherian (it is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), and $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. There is a unique polynomial $Q_X\in\mathbf Q[x]$ such that $Q_X(d)=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ for every $d\in\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic]; it is numerical, meaning $Q_X(d)\in\mathbf Z$ for every integer $d$. There exists a homogeneous ideal $J\subseteq k[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ with $X=\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_0,\ldots,z_n]/J)$ as a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_k$. For every such ideal $J$, with quotient grading as in [def-sfb-coordinate-quotient-grading], $Q_X(d)=\dim_k(k[z_0,\ldots,z_n]/J)_d$ for all sufficiently large $d\geq0$, and $Q_X$ is the unique rational polynomial with that eventual equality. No saturation assumption on $J$ is required; $J=(1)$ and $X=\varnothing$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0BEM (lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler), r=1 and F=O_X; Tag 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0); constructions.tex Tag 03GL (lemma-closed-in-projective-space); coherent.tex Tag 0AG7 (lemma-recover-tail-graded-module). Properness/Noetherianity/coherence preparation is returned proof step 1; polynomial and coordinate comparison are step 4.

proof.text: The standard opens $U_j=D_+(z_j)$ form a finite affine cover of $P=\mathbf P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$, $B=k[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$, by [def-pc-proj]. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], each $i^{-1}(U_j)$ is affine, so $X$ is quasi-compact; since the only opens of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are $\varnothing$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$, the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The convention [def-pc-projective-morphism] asks for a closed immersion into $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};\operatorname{Spec}k)=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n])$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], which is not given as $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with $R=\mathbf Z$, $S=k$, $A=\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$ and the $k$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to B$, $c\otimes T_j\mapsto cz_j$, of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]; $\beta$ sends $k\otimes A_m$ onto $B_m$ because it sends monomials to monomials of the same degree. The resulting cartesian square identifies $P$, with its structure morphism $p_B$, with $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ and its first projection. Composing $i$ with this isomorphism gives a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is projective under [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-projective-proper] to conclude properness.

source.place: Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper, with the given projective-space factorization; constructions.tex Tag 01N2, lemma-base-change-map-proj, for Proj(k[z_0,...,z_n]) = Spec k x_Z P^n_Z (Tag 01NF, definition-projective-space).

proof.text: Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its single affine ring is the field $k$, whose ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. On every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, the structure sheaf is $\widetilde R$ and is generated by $1$; it is consequently quasi-coherent of finite type by [pqf-def-coherent]. Apply [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] to obtain coherence of $\mathcal O_X$.

Put $L=i^*\mathcal O_P(1)$. The rank-one trivializations of [def-pc-projective-space-twist], pulled back using [def-pc-module-pullback], show that $L$ is invertible in the sense of [def-sc-invertible-module]. On $i^{-1}(U_j)$, the transition for $L^{\otimes d}$ is $(z_j/z_l)^d$, also for negative $d$ by taking the dual basis; it is the transition for $i^*\mathcal O_P(d)$. Sending these local bases to one another gives $L^{\otimes d}\cong\mathcal O_X(d)$ for every integer $d$. Likewise, [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] gives $\widetilde{B(d)}|_{U_j}=(B_{z_j})_d$, free with basis $z_j^d$ over $(B_{z_j})_0$, where $B=k[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$. Its transition is the same $(z_j/z_l)^d$. Thus the ambient twists used here and in the cited coordinate and section lemmas agree, including at $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 01MN, definition-twist (1); explicit degree-one chart trivializations and their transition functions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial] to the proper $k$-scheme $X$, the coherent module $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, and the single invertible module $L$. It supplies a rational numerical polynomial $Q_X$ whose value at every $d\in\mathbf Z$ is $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X\otimes L^{\otimes d})=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$, using step 3 and the tensor unit. Its values at all integers are integers, exactly the numerical assertion. No ampleness, reducedness, or nonemptiness is needed by that cited statement.

Apply [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal] with $R=k$ to the given immersion. Its explicitly defined homogeneous ideal $J$ gives $X=\operatorname{Proj}(B/J)$ as a closed subscheme of this fixed $P$; this proves existence of a defining ideal, including for empty $X$.

Now let $J$ be any homogeneous ideal with that same closed subscheme, and set $A=B/J$ with its quotient grading. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-coordinate-ring-euler-polynomial] to its quotient immersion. Because this is an identification over $P$, the twist is the same $i^*\mathcal O_P(d)$; the cited statement gives, for all $d\ge m_0$, $\dim_k A_d=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=Q_X(d)$. That statement expressly permits unsaturated $J$, the unit ideal, and empty $X$. Thus the eventual equality holds for every defining ideal, without changing the polynomial constructed in step 4.

For uniqueness, apply [lem-sfb-projective-twist-euler-section-uniqueness] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, which is quasi-coherent and has the finite presentation $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus0}\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal O_X\to0$. Step 3 and the tensor unit identify its $E_m$ with $\mathcal O_X(m)$. For $m\ge b$ its statement gives $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(m))=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$. If a rational polynomial $R$ has the same Euler values at every integer, both $R$ and $Q_X$ therefore agree eventually with this section-dimension function, so the cited uniqueness clause gives $R=Q_X$. If instead $R$ agrees eventually with $\dim_k(B/J)_m$ for any defining $J$, step 6 yields the same conclusion after taking the maximum of the finitely many thresholds. This proves both uniqueness assertions, also when the function is zero and $X$ is empty.

lean.statement: theorem exists_projectiveField_coordinateEulerPolynomial (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) {X : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Proj.projectiveSpaceOverAffine (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k) [IsClosedImmersion i] : IsProper (i ≫ Proj.projectiveSpaceOverAffineToSpec (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k) ∧ IsNoetherian X ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ∧ ∃ Q : Polynomial ℚ, (∀ d : ℤ, Q.eval (d : ℚ) = (@Scheme.Modules.eulerChar k _ X (OverClass.ofHom (i ≫ Proj.projectiveSpaceOverAffineToSpec (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k)) ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj (Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k) d)) : ℚ)) ∧ (∀ R : Polynomial ℚ, (∀ d : ℤ, R.eval (d : ℚ) = (@Scheme.Modules.eulerChar k _ X (OverClass.ofHom (i ≫ Proj.projectiveSpaceOverAffineToSpec (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k)) ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj (Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k) d)) : ℚ)) → R = Q) ∧ (∀ d : ℤ, ∃ z : ℤ, Q.eval (d : ℚ) = (z : ℚ)) ∧ (∃ J : HomogeneousIdeal (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k), ∃ e : Proj (coordinateQuotientPiece J) ≅ X, e.hom ≫ i = coordinateQuotientImmersion J) ∧ (∀ J : HomogeneousIdeal (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) k), (∃ e : Proj (coordinateQuotientPiece J) ≅ X, e.hom ≫ i = coordinateQuotientImmersion J) → (∃ b : ℕ, ∀ d : ℕ, b ≤ d → Q.eval (d : ℚ) = (Module.finrank k (coordinateQuotientPiece J d) : ℚ)) ∧ (∀ R : Polynomial ℚ, (∃ b : ℕ, ∀ d : ℕ, b ≤ d → R.eval (d : ℚ) = (Module.finrank k (coordinateQuotientPiece J d) : ℚ)) → R = Q))
